title: A leader given authority to change who instead preserves the existing order stores the demand that empowered him
body:
- A leader gains authority from a demand for change, and that demand expects release through action.
- When the leader instead preserves the existing arrangement, the demand does not resolve; he has absorbed the energy without spending it.
- The unresolved demand accumulates across his tenure, so any eventual reckoning bears a larger charge than the original grievance.
- The longer continuity is sustained in place of change, the greater the disruption when the stored demand is finally released.
- Case: a governing coalition that received a mandate for change instead protected banks over homeowners, leaving the motivating grievance intact.
conversion: A demand that empowered the leader, absorbed without being spent on actual change, accumulates into pressure that exceeds the original grievance.
